summary: Standing aside (empty trade list, neutral stance) looks reasonable given what was known: the Proposer offered nothing, the Skeptic and Implicator accepted it, and cash was only about $8 above the 10% buffer. The tape then rallied (equity +$17.13, +2.7% since the v5 start, SPY +1.65% over the same window), so we were not hurt by the stance, but the agent book (88.8% invested, +5.6% total) still trails the shadow book (99.3% invested, +7.6%); the gap is mostly the idle cash and an ETF-heavy mix, and I should not read it as proof the neutral call was wrong on one up day. The stop re-anchoring in thesis_updates (IDXX $620, DPZ $285, CARG earnings clause) was sound and followed L1/L5: closing marks are higher than the figures I used (IDXX about $700, DPZ about $341, CARG about $36.5, BTC about $80.2k), so every stop now sits further from the mark and none is close to tripping. The weakest part of the call was the CARG hold into the 11-05 after-close print: it was explicit and sized (about $3.2 for a 10% gap), but the position is now 5.5% of equity after an 8% day, so the same print risks more dollars than I computed. Distances in my reasoning were computed from stale marks and several drifted by 1-3 points by the close (BTC stop is now about 6% away, not 3.8%). BND and IEF remain the names closest to their stops (about 2% each earlier, wider after today's bond bounce). No thesis is broken at the close.
lessons: Recompute stop distances from the latest close before writing them into reasoning; marks moved 1-3 points between my read and the close, so quoted distances went stale within the day.
When holding a name through a dated earnings print (CARG 11-05), restate the dollar risk at the then-current weight after any large up day, because a rising position grows the gap risk I accepted.

Standing aside with a 10-11% cash balance is defensible when the Proposer has no candidates, but the shadow book's 99% invested lead means I should ask the Proposer next run for a named non-Technology, non-Staples candidate so idle cash has a concrete use.
Judge the neutral stance by the information at decision time, not by the +2.7% rally day; one up session neither confirms nor refutes it.
